candidates.label: Hierapolis archaeological site (Pamukkale)
candidates.support: The city's ruins beside the Pamukkale travertine terraces, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are undisputed as ancient Hierapolis; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Hierapolis was a Phrygian spa city built beside mineral hot springs near the Lycus Valley, founded, per UNESCO, by the Attalid kings of Pergamon at the end of the 2nd century BC and later flourishing under Rome. Paul's letter to the Colossians names Hierapolis alongside neighboring Colossae and Laodicea as a place where Epaphras had labored on the churches' behalf.

history.text: Hierapolis was ceded to Rome in 133 BC and, after being destroyed by an earthquake around AD 60, was rebuilt, reaching its peak of importance in the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD.

scripture.textWEB: For I testify about him that he has great zeal for you, and for those in Laodicea, and for those in Hierapolis.
